articles.title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky
articles.summary: Astronomy tourism is giving young women in Hanle income, confidence and a new role in their community.
articles.content:
It's 10pm and bitterly cold in Hanle.

Strong winds sweep across this remote village in India's Himalayan Ladakh region, but no one seems to mind. Dinner is over, yet, instead of bed, many people are gathering outside.

The reason is above them.

At 14,764ft (4,500m) above sea level, Hanle is known for its exceptionally clear, dark skies. Wrapped in thick jackets, woollen caps and gloves, tourists and visitors gather to see the Milky Way and look through telescopes at planets, the Moon and distant stars.

Among them are four young women: Palzes Angmo, Tsering Dolker, Tsering Yangdol and Padma Chamchot.

They are Hanle's astro-ambassadors, trained to guide visitors through the night sky.

By day, they cook meals, clean rooms and look after guests at their family-run homestays. By night, they set up telescopes, trace constellations with laser pointers and explain what visitors are seeing in the dark skies.

These women - all in their late 20s - grew up watching these stars, but it was only a few years ago that they learnt to study them through a telescope.

"The sky here has always been twinkling like this," 28-year-old Dolker says.

The difference today is that people travel hundreds of kilometres to see what locals have long regarded as an ordinary part of life.

articles.personality_title: Young women in India lead tourists through the stars
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Hanle is a small village high in the Himalayas of India, known for its very clear and dark night skies. This makes it a special place for astronomy, or the study of stars and planets.

**What happened** – Four young women from Hanle have become guides for tourists who come to see the stars. Each night, they set up telescopes and explain the night sky to visitors, showing planets, the Moon, and constellations. By day, they help in family-run guesthouses.

**Impact** – This new role gives the women steady income and helps them gain confidence. It also changes how people in their community see them, giving them important jobs and respect. Tourists get to enjoy the amazing sky and learn from local experts.

**What's next step** – As more visitors come, these guides may train others and help Hanle grow as a place for astronomy tourism. This can support the local economy and keep the community connected to their natural environment.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Four young women in Hanle are turning their love of the night sky into a new source of income and pride by guiding tourists through the stars.

articles.personality_title_es: Jóvenes mujeres en India guían a turistas por las estrellas
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Hanle es un pequeño pueblo en las montañas del Himalaya en India, conocido por sus cielos nocturnos muy claros y oscuros. Esto lo convierte en un lugar especial para la astronomía, el estudio de las estrellas y planetas.

**Qué pasó** – Cuatro jóvenes mujeres de Hanle se han convertido en guías para los turistas que vienen a ver las estrellas. Cada noche, montan telescopios y explican el cielo nocturno a los visitantes, mostrando planetas, la Luna y constelaciones. Durante el día, ayudan en las casas de huéspedes familiares.

**Impacto** – Este nuevo papel les da ingresos constantes y aumenta su confianza. También cambia cómo las ve la comunidad, dándoles trabajos importantes y respeto. Los turistas disfrutan del cielo increíble y aprenden de expertas locales.

**Próximo paso** – A medida que lleguen más visitantes, estas guías podrían entrenar a otras personas y ayudar a que Hanle crezca como destino de turismo astronómico. Esto puede apoyar la economía local y mantener la conexión con su entorno natural.

**Resumen en una frase** – Cuatro jóvenes mujeres en Hanle convierten su amor por el cielo nocturno en una nueva fuente de ingresos y orgullo al guiar a turistas por las estrellas.
